Thanks for the packet. Quick responses inline and a plan to close by Thursday EOD:

- Subprocessors & PII: Redwood maintains an explicit classification for each subprocessors' access. Short answer: only our telemetry aggregation service (EdgeMetrics) receives hashed identifiers and transient telemetry. Hi Samir / Helen —

Thanks for the call today. Per action items, attached is the minimal roster CSV with access-level flags and a short answers summary below.

Key points:
- KMS custody: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS keys (we integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS and bring-your-own HSM). If WellBridge supplies keys, Redwood will never export plaintext key material.
- Subprocessor access levels (from attached roster): EdgeMetrics (hashed identifiers, ephemeral logs) = read-only hashed; MetricsStore (aggregated metrics) = aggregated-only; InferencePool (runtime) = ephemeral memory only, no persistent storage of raw inputs unless explicitly requested in config.
- Retention: request traces = 30 days (configurable), aggregated model metrics = 13 months, audit logs = 25 months. We can compress retention for onshore carveout accounts to 90 days if needed and provide a signed amendment.
- Routing: Redwood guarantees contractual routing by policy. All customer-level controls can pin to US-only hosts in the Dedicated or Private deployment options; hosted fallback to other regions only occurs with explicit capacity-fallback flags and will not be used for WellBridge if you execute the onshore carveout addendum.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_delta.csv (CSV with columns: subprocessor,region,role,access_level,handles_plaintext) and a checklist for the procurement team.

I'll upload the annex draft to the shared Drive folder and loop Legal for final wording. Kim, Jordan: please confirm the annex wording for retention so I can include the 90-day option as an amendment.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Privacy PM, Redwood Inference
